item.subject: Mathematics
item.stem:
Interior Angles
Jackson was investigating the properties of polygons. Jackson made up the table below to see if he could find a connection between sides and angles.

A. Complete the table by filling in the blank spaces.

| Polygon | Number of Sides | Number of Triangles | Sum of Interior Angles |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Image: Triangle] | 3 | 1 | 1 × 180° |
| [Image: Quadrilateral] | ____ | ____ | ____ × 180° |
| [Image: Pentagon] | ____ | ____ | ____ × 180° |
| [Image: Hexagon] | ____ | ____ | ____ × 180° |

descriptors:
All entries correct
4 2 2
5 3 3
6 4 4
Incorrect (including crossed out, erased, stray marks, illegible, or off task)
Blank

item.figure_description:
A table with four rows of geometric polygons in the first column:
- Row 1: A triangle (3 sides).
- Row 2: A four-sided polygon (quadrilateral) with a dashed line segment connecting two opposite vertices, dividing the polygon into 2 triangles.
- Row 3: A five-sided polygon (pentagon) with dashed line segments drawn from one vertex to two non-adjacent vertices, dividing the polygon into 3 triangles.
- Row 4: A six-sided polygon (hexagon) with dashed line segments drawn from one vertex to three non-adjacent vertices, dividing the polygon into 4 triangles.

reference_items.figure_description:
Three geometric figures composed of small congruent right triangles:
- Figure 1: A single square with a diagonal line from the bottom-left corner to the top-right corner, dividing it into two right triangles labeled '1' (top-left) and '2' (bottom-right). Below the square is the label 'Figure 1'.
- Figure 2: A square divided into a 2-by-2 grid of 4 smaller squares. Each smaller square has a diagonal from bottom-left to top-right, creating 8 congruent triangles numbered 1 through 8: top-left square has 1 (upper) and 2 (lower); top-right square has 3 (upper) and 4 (lower); bottom-left square has 5 (upper) and 6 (lower); bottom-right square has 7 (upper) and 8 (lower). Below is the label 'Figure 2'.
- Figure 3: A square divided into a 3-by-3 grid of 9 smaller squares. Each smaller square has a diagonal from bottom-left to top-right, creating 18 congruent triangles. None of the triangles are numbered. Below is the label 'Figure 3'.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
In this figure, PQ and RS are parallel.

[Image: Parallel lines PQ and RS intersected by a transversal]

Of the following, which pair of angles has the sum of 180°?
reference_items.figure_description: Two horizontal parallel lines with arrowheads at both ends are intersected by a transversal line that slopes upward from lower-left to upper-right. The upper horizontal line has label P at its left end and Q at its right end. The lower horizontal line has label R at its left end and S at its right end. At the intersection with line PQ, four angles are numbered: angle 1 in the upper-left, angle 2 in the upper-right, angle 3 in the lower-right, and angle 4 in the lower-left. At the intersection with line RS, four angles are numbered: angle 5 in the upper-left, angle 6 in the upper-right, angle 7 in the lower-right, and angle 8 in the lower-left.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
[Image: A large triangle. The left angle is 45 degrees and the top angle is 65 degrees. A line is drawn on the side between the 45 and 64 degree angle to form two smaller triangles—one adjacent to the larger triangle, and one contained within the larger triangle. The right most angle of the triangle adjacent to the larger triangle has an angle of 30 degrees. The smaller triangle contained within the bigger triangle has an angle x that is formed by the right side of the triangle and the drawn line.]

In the figure above, what is the value of x?
reference_items.figure_description: A geometric figure featuring intersecting lines and triangles. A triangle has a horizontal base, a left side with an interior angle of 45° at the bottom-left vertex, and an interior angle of 65° at the top vertex. A line segment extends from the top vertex down to the base. A second line segment extends from a point on the left side of the triangle down and to the right, crossing the first line segment and ending at the rightmost endpoint of the extended horizontal base, where the interior angle is labeled 30°. Near the top vertex, a smaller triangle is bounded by the upper part of the left side, the upper part of the segment from the top vertex, and the crossing segment; the interior angle at the intersection of the two segments is marked with an arc and labeled x.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
Pat has red tiles and black tiles. Pat uses the tiles to make square shapes.

The 3 × 3 shape has 1 black tile and 8 red tiles.
[Image: A black tile in the middle, surrounded by the 8 red tiles, to make a square shape.]

The 4 × 4 shape has 4 black tiles and 12 red tiles.
[Image: Four black tiles forming a square in the center, with 12 red tiles lining the sides, to create a larger square shape.]

The table below shows the number of tiles for the first three shapes Pat made. Pat continued making shapes using this pattern. Complete the table for the 6 × 6 and 7 × 7 shapes.

| Shape | Number of Black Tiles | Number of Red Tiles | Total Number of Tiles |
| :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| 3 × 3 | 1 | 8 | 9 |
| 4 × 4 | 4 | 12 | 16 |
| 5 × 5 | 9 | 16 | 25 |
| 6 × 6 | 16 | | |
| 7 × 7 | 25 | | |

descriptors:
Both rows completely correct
Shape 6 x 6: 20, 36
Shape 7 x 7: 24, 49
Entries for one row correct but not both

Entries for one column correct but not both
Red Tiles: 20, 24   OR   Total Tiles: 36, 49
Other incorrect (including crossed out, erased, stray marks, illegible, or off task)

reference_items.figure_description:
Two square shapes made of smaller square tiles and an explanatory key:
- A 3 × 3 shape composed of 9 tiles: 1 black center tile labeled 'B' surrounded by 8 gray tiles labeled 'R'.
- A 4 × 4 shape composed of 16 tiles: 4 black center tiles arranged in a 2 × 2 square, each labeled 'B', surrounded by 12 gray tiles labeled 'R'.
- A key below the 3 × 3 shape shows a black square labeled 'B' = Black tile, and a gray square labeled 'R' = Red tile.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
Pat wanted to add a line to the table showing how to find the number of tiles needed to make a square of any size. Use the patterns in the table on the opposite page to help you complete the line for shape n × n in the table below.

| Shape | Number of Black Tiles | Number of Red Tiles | Total Number of Tiles |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| n × n | (n − 2)^2 | | |

descriptors:
Both expressions correct in simplified form
Red tiles: 4(n − 1); 4n − 4; or correct verbal expression
Total tiles: n^2, n x n; or correct verbal expression, such as “square the number” or “multiply by itself”
Both expressions correct with expression for red tiles in the form of total number of tiles minus number of black tiles e.g., n^2 − (n − 2)^2 or equivalent.
Expression for red tiles correct as in 20 but not expression for total tiles
Expression for total tiles correct as in 20 but not expression for red tiles
Incorrect expression including n for red tiles or total or both (includes incorrect attempts to express red tiles as difference from total tiles)
Other incorrect (including crossed out, erased, stray marks, illegible, or off task)

reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
[Image: Two parallel lines, M and N. M lies above N. Two lines are drawn over M and N. One goes up from the left to the right, and the other one goes down, from the left to the right. The two lines intersect N at two different points, but meet at a common point on line M. This forms a triangle between lines M and N. The top angle of this triangle is angle B. The right most angle of this triangle is 70 degrees. The line that goes up from the left to the right intersects line M at a 60 degree angle.]

Lines m and n are parallel.

What is the value of b?

Answer: ____

descriptors: Incorrect (including crossed out, erased, stray marks, illegible, or off task)

reference_items.figure_description: Two horizontal parallel lines with arrows at both ends are labeled m (top line) and n (bottom line). Two intersecting lines cross lines m and n: one line slopes upward from lower left to upper right, and the other slopes downward from upper left to lower right. The two lines intersect each other at a single point on line m, and they cross line n at two separate points, forming a triangle between lines m and n. The top interior angle of this triangle at the intersection point on line m is marked with an arc and labeled b°. The bottom-right interior angle of the triangle along line n is marked with an arc and labeled 70°. Above line m, in the angle between the right side of line m and the upward-sloping line, the angle is marked with an arc and labeled 60°.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 eighth-grade mathematics data.

slope.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the two-parameter logistic (2PL) model, which TIMSS uses for constructed-response items worth 1 point, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (eighth-grade mathematics)". What is the item's slope (discrimination) parameter a? A higher a means that the item separates students of lower and higher mathematics ability more sharply. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.
